$comment: Basics: what two implementations need in common that is neither a Trust Task nor a ceremony (identifiers, carriers, the document framework, group keys, devices, registries). Each names what a project brings (requires) and what has to happen between two projects (done). Runs test them like credentials, tasks and ceremonies.

layers.title: The person
layers.asks: Who is this, across devices and apps?

layers.title: Wire and documents
layers.asks: Does a sealed message arrive, and does the other side read what arrives?

layers.title: Membership
layers.asks: Who says someone belongs, and who reads it?

layers.title: Shared state
layers.asks: Can several apps hold the same group data, offline too and after a lost device?

layers.title: Networks
layers.asks: How do communities recognise one another?

basics.title: Identifier resolution across apps
basics.asks: Each side resolves the other's DID method and finds its keys.
requires: Both sides: an identifier under a DID method, and signatures with a key the DID resolves to
Each side: resolves the other side's DID method
basics.done: Each side verifies a signature the other side made under its DID, using keys from its own resolution of that DID.

basics.title: Several devices, one person
basics.asks: A person's devices act for the same person toward other apps, and a lost or restored device does not break the relationship.
requires: Person side: several devices under one person, each with a key of its own
Counterpart app: a relationship with the person, not with one device
basics.done: The counterpart app treats a person's second device as the same relationship, and a restored device continues it without a new ceremony.

basics.title: Delivery through one carrier
basics.asks: Two apps reach each other through the same mediator or relay.
requires: Both apps: speak the carrier's wire protocol (TSP for the VTI mediator) and have a relationship or an account at the same carrier; a passing run of tsp-conformance shows the wire side
Both apps: seal and open messages for the other side's identifier
basics.done: A sealed message from one app arrives at the other through one carrier and opens, in both directions.
basics.origin: tsp-conformance, VTI; wire conformance from OpenVTC tsp-conformance

basics.title: Delivery across carriers
basics.asks: Two parties at different mediators or relays still reach each other.
requires: Each app: reachable at a carrier of its own
The carriers: forward to one another, or one app reaches both
basics.done: A sealed message from one app at one carrier arrives at the other app at another carrier and opens, in both directions.

basics.title: Common document framework
basics.asks: Wire artifacts are Trust Task documents with type URI, schema and proof the other side can check.
requires: Each side: emits its wire artifacts as Trust Task documents with a type URI, a schema and a proof
Each side: parses foreign Trust Task documents, with a shared library or its own
basics.done: A document emitted by one app parses in the other as a Trust Task document and its proof verifies, even where the receiver does not know the type.
basics.origin: DTGWG Trust Tasks framework; document conformance (shared vectors and runner) from the Trust Tasks task force and the Weave one-pager

basics.title: Error and status answers
basics.asks: A receiver that cannot process a document answers in a form the sender reads.
requires: Receiving side: answers a document it cannot process with trust-task-error
Sending side: reads trust-task-error and shows it or acts on it
basics.done: One app sends a document the other cannot process; the answer is a trust-task-error the sender reads, and the sender's state afterwards matches the error.

basics.title: Interop with traditional tools
basics.asks: A group governed in the trust substrate is used by a conventional tool (calendar, forum, folder) that only asks who belongs.
requires: Group side: a membership statement or an authorization view that answers who belongs
Tool side: a conventional tool that grants access on that answer
basics.done: A conventional tool grants access to a group governed in the trust substrate, asking only who belongs.
basics.origin: Weave one-pager (how decentralized tools interoperate with traditional ones)

basics.title: Same group in two apps
basics.asks: Several apps read and write the same encrypted shared state of one community.
requires: Host side: a group whose shared state is encrypted under one group key agreement at the boundary (MLS 1.0, ciphersuite 0x0001), joinable by welcome or invitation
Joining side: a client of its own implementation that joins, reads and writes
basics.done: A client of one implementation joins a group hosted by another, reads the records already there and writes one the host reads back. A procedure may run it with the writer offline when writing: the record arrives later and the host accepts it as of its issue time.
basics.origin: Weave deck, Level 2a; one-pager (being in the same group in two different apps); key agreement at the boundary from rltp (E13)

basics.title: History for newcomers
basics.asks: A member admitted later reads what the group wrote before, as far as the group allows.
requires: Both sides: shared-room
Host side: keeps earlier epochs or keys for newcomers, as far as the group allows
basics.done: A member admitted later from the other app reads what the group wrote before the admission, within what the group allows, and nothing beyond.

basics.title: Recovery after a captured device
basics.asks: Removing a device ends its access to future group content on every app.
requires: Both sides: shared-room or key-agreement
Removing side: removes a device from the group and rotates the group key
basics.done: After one app removes a device, content written afterwards in either app does not open on that device.

basics.title: Registry lookup
basics.asks: Two communities recognise each other through a registry.
requires: Registry side: a registry that answers whether a community is recognised, as a Trust Task or an equivalent
Querying side: asks the registry before trusting a statement from a community it does not know
basics.done: One community accepts a statement from another it does not know because a registry both read recognises it.

basics.title: Networks of communities
basics.asks: A community recognises a member of a community it does not know, through a third community both know.
requires: Three communities: a statement of recognition from the third to each of the other two (registry-lookup or membership-statement)
Accepting side: follows the chain of recognition
basics.done: A community accepts a membership statement of a community it has no direct relation with, through one it has.

statusWords.stated: the project says so in its own public texts or code we could point at, read by someone else; the row has not been confirmed by the project
statusWords.runs: the project meets the requirements in code or a live service another project can exercise today; not yet a run between two projects
statusWords.vectors: byte-exact test vectors published, re-derivable by a shared runner, not yet exercised against another implementation
statusWords.open: the project knows the gap and says so
statusWords.n/a: the project does not aim at this scenario, with a reason
